activities.anchor: Think about what a salon actually is.
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the spotless implement
activities.name: cosmoSpotPredict

config.q: The implement in your hand looks spotless. What do you know for certain?
choices: Nothing about its microbe load — cleanliness you can see is not cleanliness you can trust
It is safe, since nothing is visible on it
It is sterile, because it looks clean
That it was disinfected within the last hour
config.why: None of it is visible: bacteria in a foot bath, a virus on a reused implement, a fungus on a porous nail file — the regimen, not the look, decides.

activities.anchor: Their existence is why the control ladder has a top rung at all.
activities.caption: pair each salon signature with its microbe
activities.name: cosmoMicrobeMatch

config.prompt: Pair each salon signature with the organism behind it:

pairs.left: green discolouration on nails kept damp under enhancements
the 2000 foot-spa boils outbreak in California
pairs.right: Mycobacterium fortuitum, slow-growing in whirlpool lines

pairs.left: folliculitis and boils over broken skin
dormant forms that shrug off drying and disinfection

config.why: Standing water and product residue are the two best nurseries — which is why the regimen starts with cleaning.

activities.anchor: prevention by barriers and disinfection is the entire defence
activities.caption: true or false — the viral rulebook
activities.name: cosmoVirusJudge

statements.s: A virus multiplies happily on a doorknob between clients.
statements.why: It can survive on one long enough to transfer, but reproduction needs a living cell.

statements.s: Antibiotics are a valid response to a viral client infection.
statements.why: They interrupt bacterial life processes; a virus has none to interrupt.

statements.s: Hepatitis B can survive on implements for days.
statements.why: Bloodborne and hardy — which is why the industry recommends the vaccine.

statements.s: Universal precautions treat all blood as infectious, regardless of how healthy the client looks.
statements.why: You cannot see who carries what — so every client, every service, gets the same guard.

activities.caption: a suspicious patch at the consultation — walk it
activities.name: cosmoFungusBranch

config.root: During the consultation you notice a suspicious patch on the scalp.

start.text: Fungi travel through damp floors, shared towels, combs and clippers. First call?

choices.label: Refuse the service, explain why, refer to a physician
choices.feedback: The regulation's own call: no service over an active infection — and the referral is care, not rejection.

choices.label: Work around it carefully with gloves
choices.feedback: Onychomycosis thrives under enhancements applied over it — no amount of care near a colony is safe.

work.text: Improvised treatment and careful work-arounds both spread it — the board expects refusal plus referral.

refer.text: Referred. The client asks why you will not just treat it here.

choices.label: Diagnosis and treatment exceed the licence — refusal plus referral is the standard
choices.feedback: Scope of practice: exclusion rules and referral are what the regulations standardise.

choices.label: Offer an antifungal product from the shelf
choices.feedback: Same trap, product flavour — improvising a treatment is outside the licence.

product.text: Outside the licence — the refusal plus referral IS the standard of care.

scope.text: Exclusion until clear, referral for diagnosis — board regulations, not rudeness.

config.why: Dry floors, no shared porous implements, refusal plus referral — the discipline is environmental.

activities.anchor: destroys most pathogens on hard, non-porous surfaces — metal, plastic, glass
activities.caption: one multi-use tool, one full sequence
activities.name: cosmoSeqOrder

config.prompt: After every client, one multi-use tool's full sequence — put it in order:
items: Disinfect — visibly wet for the label's full contact time
config.why: The ladder is ordered by what it kills — but the wet duration, not the bottle, earns the claim.

activities.caption: call the wet time that earns the kill claim
activities.name: cosmoContactEst

config.prompt: The label's contact time — how long must a disinfected surface stay visibly wet, often?
config.why: Often ten minutes — the wet duration, not the spraying, earns the kill claim; a skipped wash leaves film the chemistry cannot penetrate.
config.context: Five seconds of mist and a dry towel is theatre, not decontamination.

activities.anchor: Pedicure whirlpool baths carry their own regime
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the foot-spa regime
activities.name: cosmoWhirlSpot

config.prompt: One of these foot-spa claims is wrong — click it:
lines: Biofilm — microbes sealed in a slimy layer — clings to pipes and screens and resists casual disinfection.
Screens and jets are disassembled, cleaned and disinfected between clients and nightly.
The regime's logs are optional paperwork in every jurisdiction.
In 2000, more than a hundred customers of one California salon developed leg boils from contaminated foot baths.
Each documented case became a regulation — the rules are scar tissue.
config.correction: Recorded logs are legally required in many jurisdictions — the organisms wrote the rules.
config.why: Hepatitis B through reused implements, folliculitis from unsanitised clippers, ringworm from shared tools — every rule descends from a documented case.

activities.anchor: The components translate directly behind the chair
activities.caption: two disciplines at the station — file each fact
activities.name: cosmoPrecautionSort

config.prompt: Two disciplines at the station — file each fact:

items.label: the single most important and effective measure in infection control
task-specific and single-use — one pair per client
protects the wearer, not the next client
before, between and after client contacts
where the great majority of healthcare-associated infections travel

config.why: Gloves protect the wearer; hands carry the infections — hygiene after every removal is the whole point.
